physicssimulation.name: Physics Simulation: The Engine Behind Reality

physicssimulation.description: From F=ma to fluid dynamics. Five maps covering the full stack of physics simulation: the mathematical foundations (integration methods), rigid body dynamics (collisions and constraints), elastic systems (springs and cloth), force fields (particles and n-body), and continuous matter (fluids and soft bodies). Each map adds a layer of complexity â€” and a new way the simulation can break.
learning_objectives: Numerical integration: Euler, Verlet, RK4 â€” and why the method matters
Rigid body dynamics: rotation, angular momentum, inertia tensors
Collision detection: broad phase (spatial hashing) and narrow phase (GJK/SAT)
Constraints: joints, hinges, and how physics engines solve them
Spring-mass systems: Hooke's law, damping, and emergent cloth behavior
Force fields and vector fields: invisible forces made visible
N-body simulation: gravitational democracy and the three-body problem
SPH fluid simulation: discretizing continuous matter into particles
Finite Element Method: engineering simulation for deformable bodies
Soft body physics: the compromise between rigid and fluid
content: PhysicsSim_Foundations: Discretizing Reality — Newton’s laws → numerical integration → Verlet. The math that makes simulation possible.
PhysicsSim_Bodies: Rigid Bodies and Contact — Rigid bodies → collision detection → constraints → bouncing ball. Solid things interacting.
PhysicsSim_Springs: Elasticity and Memory — Mass-spring-damper → spring networks → cloth. Elastic connections and emergent softness.
PhysicsSim_Fields: Invisible Architecture — Force fields → vector fields → particles → n-body → three-body problem. Invisible forces, visible chaos.
PhysicsSim_Continuum: Continuous Matter — Fluid (SPH) → FEM → soft bodies → magnetic fields → kinetic sculpture. Continuous matter, discrete approximation.

artifact_groups.rationale: Newton's laws launch the pipeline: force produces acceleration, integration methods (Euler vs Verlet) translate continuous math into discrete timesteps. The foundation of every physics engine. Simulation instability completes the picture — watch what happens when dt grows too large.

Solid objects meeting: rigid body rotation and angular momentum, collision detection (broad/narrow phase), constraints limiting freedom, bouncing ball as simplest negotiation between velocity and restitution.
Hooke's law scaled up: single spring-damper oscillation, spring-mass lattices propagating waves, cloth emerging from many springs solving equilibrium collectively.
Invisible architecture: force fields and vector fields directing particles, n-body gravitational democracy, three-body chaos where determinism meets unpredictability.
Continuous matter discretized: SPH fluid particles, FEM stress-strain, soft body deformation, magnetic fields, and kinetic sculpture where physics becomes art.
Coefficient of restitution in action: elastic vs inelastic collisions, energy loss per bounce. Every bounce negotiates between velocity and entropy.
Spring-mass lattice at scale: thousands of Hooke's law connections draping, tearing, settling. Cloth thinks with its whole body — no vertex knows the shape.
Broad phase meets narrow phase: spatial hashing eliminates distant pairs, GJK/SAT resolve overlaps. Split arena mirrors the two-stage detection pipeline.
Joints, hinges, degrees of freedom: the constraint solver reduces motion to what's permitted. Scaffold room with ramps embodies structured limitation.
Discretization as engineering truth: finite basis functions approximate continuous stress-strain. Laboratory setting matches the analytical precision of FEM.
Two approaches to fluid: lattice gas automata (discrete collision rules on a grid) and SPH (smoothed particle hydrodynamics). Different discretizations of the same continuous truth.
Force as spatial function: radial room descends toward center source. Particles read invisible gradient — divergence, convergence, and vortex made walkable.
Oscillation dissected: underdamped rings, overdamped creeps, critically damped settles fastest. Corridor with spring-mounted platforms embodies the damping ratio.
Three laws, one arena: inertia resists, F=ma accelerates, action-reaction pairs. The simplest rules constraining everything physics simulation builds upon.
Stepped ascending room as accumulated area: Euler's first-order error, Verlet's time-reversible elegance, RK4's precision. The timestep method determines whether simulation behaves or explodes.
Particle emitters, life cycles, and collective behavior from simple birth-death rules. Many particles, one system.
Inertia tensor and angular momentum: obstacle course where rigid bodies tumble, spin, and conserve rotational energy. Geometry determines resistance to rotation.
Suspended walkway as spring-mass bridge: local springs propagating waves globally. The discrete secret of continuous matter — vibration traveling through connected nodes.
Poincaré’s impossibility: three gravitational bodies with no closed-form solution. Deterministic chaos — predictable rules, unpredictable outcomes.
Space as instruction set: vector field arrows direct particles through sources, sinks, and vortices. Dark sphere anchors the visual field; streamlines reveal invisible architecture.
Verlet's elegance isolated: position-based integration that is time-reversible, energy-conserving, and stable. The method that makes cloth and molecular dynamics possible.
